key_insight: The paper reframes hyperparameter tuning as an interpretable game-theoretic analysis, using Shapley Effects and Pareto fronts to identify which hyperparameters most strongly influence different objectives.
engineering_relevance: It helps practitioners narrow the search space, prioritize impactful hyperparameters, and evaluate models early in multi-objective neural network workflows.
method: Apply Shapley Effects for global hyperparameter sensitivity analysis.
Use Pareto front sets to find effective hyperparameter configurations.
Interpret objective-specific interactions across different neural network architectures.
evidence_signal: The framework is demonstrated on three distinct neural network architectures across different problem domains under multi-objective settings.
watch_item: Results are interpretive and problem-dependent, so sensitivity rankings and Pareto conclusions may not transfer across datasets, objectives, or model families without re-analysis.
paper_title: Which Hyperparameters Matter? A Game-Theoretic Framework for Interpretable Hyperparameter Sensitivity Analysis
